name: SourceForge

sources.title: SourceForge 'Create a Project' page — name, URL slug, tool selection, ToS

requirements: A SourceForge account is required ('Login Required' gate on the create page; registration at /user/registration)
Aimed at open-source projects — Git/Mercurial/Subversion, tickets, wiki, forums, mailing lists, file-release mirrors, web hosting
Must agree to Slashdot Media Terms of Use; non-compliant projects are removed
Business-software listings are a separate surface (sourceforge.net/software/vendors)
preparation: Project name and a desired short URL name (project lives at sourceforge.net/p/<slug>)
Which tools to enable: Git/Hg/SVN, file downloads + stats via the mirror network, tickets, wiki, forums, blog, mailing lists, free web hosting at a sourceforge.io subdomain or custom domain
Alternatively: a GitHub repo to import wholesale via /p/import_project/github/ (Bitbucket/GitLab via the project's Import page after creation)
workflow: Enter project name and URL slug
Select the tools the project needs
Check the Terms of Use box and submit
Optionally run the GitHub importer or configure the project's Import page for other forges
watchFor: Two honeypot fields on the form ('You seem to have CSS turned off. Please don't fill out this field.') — automated submitters must leave them empty
The open-source project forge and the business-software directory are different products — a SaaS listing belongs on the /software/ vendor side, not as a /p/ project
Project URL names are a global namespace — first-come slug
ToS compliance is enforced with removal
countsAsLive: The project page at sourceforge.net/p/<slug> (or /projects/<name>) resolves publicly and accepts tool configuration.
unknowns: Whether new projects undergo any manual review before appearing in directory/search pages
Whether the business-software vendor listing (separate flow) has a cost
